title: Finite element study of the efficacy of three different loops for bodily protraction of the mandibular molar
venue: Scientific Reports 15 (1), 13938
label: Journal article
summary: A finite-element model built from a patient CBCT scan compares T, Cherry and open helical loops at 10°, 15° and 20° tip-back for protracting the mandibular second molar. All three loops performed alike; a 15° tip-back moved the molar with negligible tipping and no extrusion or intrusion.
imageAlt: Finite-element models of the molar with the T loop, Cherry loop and open helical loop.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Mehta et al., Scientific Reports (2025), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

title: Secondary Wake Mode Instability Analysis Behind Two-Dimensional Cylinder Using OpenFOAM®
venue: Proceedings of Fluid Mechanics and Fluid Power (FMFP) 2023, Vol. 1: Fluid Mechanics, Springer, pp. 483–493
label: Conference chapter
summary: Uses OpenFOAM to examine the secondary wake mode instability in the flow behind a two-dimensional cylinder.
imageAlt: Smoke visualisation of a Kármán vortex street behind a cylinder.
imageCredit: Illustrative photo: Jürgen Wagner, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

title: Understanding the role of CFD in microwave-assisted pyrolysis for biomass conversion
venue: Journal of Analytical and Applied Pyrolysis 179, 106477
label: Journal article
summary: Reviews how CFD helps explain microwave-assisted pyrolysis of biomass, including microwave absorption and the distribution of thermal and electromagnetic fields. It identifies research gaps and argues for pairing simulations with experiments to predict bio-oil, biochar and syngas yields.
imageAlt: A pile of biochar.
imageCredit: Illustrative photo: Oregon Department of Forestry, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

title: Phase Change Material Applications in Thermal Management of Electronics and Electrical Systems
venue: Phase Change Materials for Thermal Energy Management and Storage, CRC Press, pp. 207–230
label: Book chapter
summary: Reviews phase change materials for cooling high-power-density electronics: passive options such as PCM-enhanced heat sinks, heat pipes and thermal interface materials, and hybrid systems that pair PCMs with air, liquid or thermoelectric cooling.
imageAlt: A CPU heat sink with copper heat pipes and a fan.
imageCredit: Illustrative photo: Hustvedt, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

title: Advances in computational fluid dynamics modeling for biomass pyrolysis: a review
venue: Energies 16 (23), 7839
label: Journal article
summary: A review of CFD modelling for biomass pyrolysis in conventional and microwave-assisted reactors: reaction kinetics and governing equations, the role of microwave wavelength and penetration depth, and the main modelling challenges, with directions for future work.
imageAlt: Diagram linking pyrolysis variables, CFD quantities and optimisation outcomes.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Kulkarni et al., Energies (2023), CC BY 4.0

title: Entropy analysis of the MHD Jeffrey fluid flow in an inclined porous pipe with convective boundaries
venue: International Journal of Thermofluids 17, 100275
label: Journal article
summary: Entropy generation in mixed-convection flow of a non-Newtonian Jeffrey fluid through an inclined porous pipe with convective walls under a magnetic field. Entropy generation and Bejan numbers are mapped against the Hartmann, Darcy, Grashof, Brinkman and Biot numbers.
imageAlt: Schematic of Jeffrey fluid flow in an inclined circular pipe.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Raje et al., International Journal of Thermofluids (2023), CC BY 4.0

title: Recent advancements of CFD and heat transfer studies in pyrolysis: a review
venue: Journal of Analytical and Applied Pyrolysis 175, 106163
label: Journal article
summary: A critical review of fluid-flow and heat-transport modelling in conventional, microwave-assisted and solar-assisted pyrolysis reactors. It concludes that CFD models need better validation and accuracy, and sets out steps to broaden their use.
imageAlt: Graphical abstract linking pyrolysis reactor types to CFD model categories.
imageCredit: Graphical abstract, Dadi et al., Journal of Analytical and Applied Pyrolysis (2023), © Elsevier

title: Significance of a permeable semi-circular body and magnetic field on the double-diffusive traits
venue: International Journal of Thermofluids 20, 100486
label: Journal article
summary: Lattice Boltzmann simulations of double-diffusive natural convection around a heated, permeable semi-circular body in a cold square enclosure under a magnetic field. Raising buoyancy, permeability and the field angle improves heat and mass transfer.
imageAlt: Schematic of a permeable semi-circular body in a square enclosure with an inclined magnetic field.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Vijaybabu et al., International Journal of Thermofluids (2023), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

title: Two-step synthesis of biochar using torrefaction and microwave-assisted pyrolysis: understanding the effects of torrefaction temperature and catalyst loading
venue: Journal of Analytical and Applied Pyrolysis 175, 106191
label: Journal article
summary: Sawdust torrefied at 125–175 °C was converted to biochar by microwave-assisted pyrolysis with a graphite susceptor and a KOH catalyst, giving biochar yields of 24.2–48.1 wt%.
imageAlt: Graphical abstract: sawdust torrefaction, microwave pyrolysis and biochar characterisation.
imageCredit: Graphical abstract, Potnuri et al., Journal of Analytical and Applied Pyrolysis (2023), © Elsevier

title: Irreversibility and hydrothermal analysis of the MWCNTs/GNPs-based nanofluids for electronics cooling applications of the pin-fin heat sinks: Multiphase Eulerian-Lagrangian modeling
venue: Case Studies in Thermal Engineering 31, 101806
label: Journal article
summary: Eulerian–Lagrangian simulations of MWCNT and MWCNT/graphene-nanoplatelet nanofluids in pin-fin heat sinks for electronics cooling. Triangular fins dissipated the most heat; rhombus fins scored best overall because of their lower pressure drop.
imageAlt: Pin-fin heat sink with triangular, rhombus and hydrofoil fin configurations.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Ambreen et al., Case Studies in Thermal Engineering (2022), CC BY 4.0

title: Numerical analysis of the performance improvement of a flat-plate solar collector using conjugated porous blocks
venue: Renewable Energy 172, 382-391
label: Journal article
summary: OpenFOAM simulations of a direct-absorption flat-plate solar collector with three conjugated porous blocks along the insulated bottom wall. The blocks push flow toward the absorber plate; performance is best with a short block at the inlet and a tall one at the outlet.
imageAlt: Solar collector channel with three metal-foam blocks along the bottom wall.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Anirudh & Dhinakaran, Renewable Energy (2021), © Elsevier

title: Numerical investigation of unsteady flow across tandem square cylinders near a moving wall at Re= 100
venue: Case Studies in Thermal Engineering 26, 101042
label: Journal article
summary: Flow past two tandem square cylinders near a moving wall at Re = 100, for spacing ratios 0.5–8 and wall-gap ratios 0.1–4. The moving wall largely decides when vortex shedding starts and stops; drag is highest on a lone cylinder and lowest on the downstream one.
imageAlt: Computational domain with upstream and downstream square cylinders above a moving wall.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Rajpoot et al., Case Studies in Thermal Engineering (2021), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

title: On the effects of orientation on flow and heat transfer from a semi-circular cylinder near a stationary wall
venue: Case Studies in Thermal Engineering 26, 100967
label: Journal article
summary: Forced convection from a heated semi-circular cylinder in the shear layer of a stationary wall, with its curved or flat face upstream, at Re = 100–200 and gap ratios 0.1–0.5. The curved-forebody orientation gives the largest heat-transfer enhancement; Nusselt number correlations are provided.
imageAlt: Domain with a heated semi-circular cylinder near a wall, shown in two orientations.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Rajpoot et al., Case Studies in Thermal Engineering (2021), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

title: Phase Change Materials and Its Applications
venue: Fundamentals and Innovations in Solar Energy, Springer, pp. 311–340
label: Book chapter
summary: A book chapter on phase change materials: types, properties and enhancement techniques, modelling approaches, and applications in buildings, thermal management of batteries, electronics and photovoltaics, and high-temperature solar thermal storage.
imageAlt: Temperature against energy content as a phase change material melts and solidifies.
imageCredit: Illustrative diagram, Wikimedia Commons, CC0

title: Numerical study on performance improvement of a flat-plate solar collector filled with porous foam
venue: Renewable Energy 147, 1704-1717
label: Journal article
summary: OpenFOAM study of a flat-plate solar collector channel filled with porous metal foam, modelling radiation with the Rosseland approximation and buoyancy at inclinations up to 45°. The foam improves thermal mixing, and the largest gains come at intermediate tilt angles.
imageAlt: Inclined solar collector channel filled with metal foam.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Anirudh & Dhinakaran, Renewable Energy (2020), © Elsevier

title: Performance improvement of a flat-plate solar collector by inserting intermittent porous blocks
venue: Renewable Energy 145, 428-441
label: Journal article
summary: Intermittent porous metal-foam blocks in a flat-plate solar collector, studied in OpenFOAM across block arrangements, counts, heights and permeabilities. More blocks improve mixing but cost pressure drop; a few short blocks perform best overall, ahead of a continuous porous layer.
imageAlt: Solar collector channel with intermittent metal-foam blocks in four arrangements.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Anirudh & Dhinakaran, Renewable Energy (2020), © Elsevier

title: Effects of Prandtl number on the forced convection heat transfer from a porous square cylinder
venue: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer 126, 1358-1375
label: Journal article
summary: Forced convection from a porous square cylinder for Prandtl numbers 0.71–100, Re = 1–40 and Da = 10⁻⁶–10⁻², using a modified OpenFOAM solver with the Darcy–Brinkman–Forchheimer model. Correlations for the mean Nusselt number are provided.
imageAlt: Electronics cooling loop with a porous block above LED chips.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Anirudh & Dhinakaran, International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer (2018), © Elsevier

title: Lattice Boltzmann simulations of flow and heat transfer from a permeable triangular cylinder under the influence of aiding buoyancy
venue: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer 117, 799-817
label: Journal article
summary: Lattice Boltzmann simulations of flow and heat transfer from a heated permeable triangular cylinder in upward flow with aiding buoyancy, comparing apex-facing and side-facing orientations.
imageAlt: Domain for upward flow past a heated permeable triangular cylinder in two orientations.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Vijaybabu et al., International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer (2018), © Elsevier

title: LBM simulation of unsteady flow and heat transfer from a diamond-shaped porous cylinder
venue: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer 120, 267-283
label: Journal article
summary: Lattice Boltzmann simulations of unsteady flow and heat transfer from a heated, diamond-shaped porous cylinder, motivated by porous pin-fin arrangements for cooling power devices.
imageAlt: Porous pin-fin cooling application and the domain around a diamond-shaped porous cylinder.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Vijaybabu et al., International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer (2018), © Elsevier

title: On the onset of vortex shedding past a two-dimensional porous square cylinder
venue: Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics 179, 200-214
label: Journal article
summary: Locates the onset of vortex shedding behind a porous square cylinder for 41 ≤ Re ≤ 50 across a range of permeability and porosity, using OpenFOAM with the Darcy–Brinkman–Forchheimer model. A shedding-frequency correlation is given, with unsteady results up to Re = 150.
imageAlt: Computational domain around a porous square cylinder in uniform flow.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Anirudh & Dhinakaran, Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics (2018), © Elsevier

title: Mixed convective heat transfer from a permeable square cylinder: A lattice Boltzmann analysis
venue: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer 115, 854-870
label: Journal article
summary: Lattice Boltzmann analysis of mixed convection from a heated permeable square cylinder in vertical upward flow, motivated by reactor-core fuel and control-rod arrays treated as a porous bluff body.
imageAlt: Nuclear reactor core whose fuel and control-rod array is modelled as a porous bluff body.
imageCredit: Figure 1, Vijaybabu et al., International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer (2017), © Elsevier
